name: Crypt wall corner
description: An L-shaped corner of crypt wall, 0.6 m thick and 3 m high, in the cool, dark dressed ashlar of the crypt wall section: long quoins alternate between the arms over a square corner pier, worn rounded arrises over dark recessed joints, a slightly proud footing course and a plain coping. One arm runs 0.75 m from the corner to +x, the other to +y, where they meet straight sections. Damp darkens the footing and streaks the outer faces.

provenance.prompt: An L-shaped corner of the same crypt wall as wall_crypt_straight (dark dressed ashlar, about 3 m high and 0.6 m thick): two half-sections, one arm from the centre to the +x edge, the other from the centre to the +y edge, joined at a square corner pier, so it meets straight 1.5 m sections. Cooler and darker than the village fieldstone, with worn joints and a little damp staining.
